Create a production-ready single-file website in one html file.

GOAL
Build a premium event landing page for **“ARTIFACT: Museum Night”** — a ticketed night museum event with ticket selection, but no real payment.

TECH / STRICT
- One html file only.
- HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript only.
- No frameworks.
- No libraries.
- Inline CSS and inline JS.
- Remote images are allowed.
- Must work by opening the file directly in a browser.

DESIGN DIRECTION
Create a visually striking cinematic museum-night website.

The design should feel like:
- luxury museum after dark
- velvet darkness
- golden spotlights
- quiet mystery
- art-house cinema
- premium cultural event

Visual style:
- dark velvet / near-black background
- deep burgundy and midnight navy gradients
- soft spotlight effects
- elegant serif headlines
- modern readable sans-serif body text
- thin gold dividers
- subtle grain/noise overlay using CSS only
- large editorial hero layout
- asymmetric image cards
- glass-like dark panels
- premium ticket cards
- smooth hover states
- scroll reveal animations
- strong typography hierarchy

Color palette:
- Background: `#070506`
- Velvet: `#1a0710`
- Burgundy: `#3a0f1d`
- Midnight navy: `#07111f`
- Gold: `#d6ad60`
- Soft gold: `#f3d79b`
- Ivory text: `#f8efe2`
- Muted text: `#b9a999`
- Panel: `rgba(255, 244, 220, 0.06)`
- Border: `rgba(214, 173, 96, 0.28)`

TYPOGRAPHY
Use CSS font stacks only:
- Headlines: `Georgia`, `Times New Roman`, serif
- Body: `Inter`, `system-ui`, `Segoe UI`, sans-serif

LAYOUT
Single-page landing with sticky navbar and smooth scrolling.

SECTIONS

1. Navbar
- Logo: ARTIFACT
- Links:
  - Program
  - Artists
  - Venue
  - Tickets
  - FAQ
- CTA button: “Get Tickets”
- Active nav state while scrolling
- Mobile responsive menu

2. Hero
- Full cinematic hero section
- Large serif headline:
  “Museum Night, Reimagined”
- Event name:
  “ARTIFACT: Museum Night”
- Date/time/place:
  - 18 October 2026
  - 19:00–02:00
  - The Old Gallery, Warsaw
- CTAs:

- <title>ARTIFACT: Museum Night — 18 October 2026, The Old Gallery, Warsaw</title>

- Favicon: inline SVG data URI — a small gold diamond/artifact glyph on dark background, e.g. <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,..."> with URL-encoded SVG (gold #d6ad60 shape on #070506).

=== DESIGN SYSTEM (CSS custom properties on :root) ===
--bg:#070506; --velvet:#1a0710; --burgundy:#3a0f1d; --navy:#07111f; --gold:#d6ad60; --gold-soft:#f3d79b; --ivory:#f8efe2; --muted:#b9a999; --panel:rgba(255,244,220,.06); --border:rgba(214,173,96,.28);

Global look: near-black velvet background; deep burgundy + midnight navy radial/linear gradients; soft golden spotlight effects (large radial-gradient glows, position fixed or absolute, pointer-events:none); thin gold divider lines (1px, gradient gold fading at edges); subtle film-grain/noise overlay covering the whole page using CSS ONLY — implement as a fixed full-viewport overlay div/pseudo-element with an inline SVG feTurbulence data-URI background, low opacity (~0.05), pointer-events:none, z-index high but below modals; glass-like dark panels (background:var(--panel); backdrop-filter:blur(10px); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius); strong typography hierarchy (eyebrow labels in letter-spaced uppercase gold small text, huge serif section titles, muted body copy); smooth hover states everywhere (translateY lifts, gold border glow, shadow); scroll-reveal animations via IntersectionObserver adding a .visible class (fade + translateY, with transition); respect prefers-reduced-motion (disable reveal transitions/animations); smooth scrolling (html{scroll-behavior:smooth} with scroll-padding-top for the sticky nav height). Buttons: visible hover AND :focus-visible states (gold outline). Fully responsive with mobile breakpoints (~900px and ~640px).

=== SECTIONS (single-page, sticky navbar, smooth scrolling) ===

1) NAVBAR (sticky/fixed top, glass dark background with blur + thin gold bottom border): Logo text "ARTIFACT" (serif, letter-spaced, gold, with a small diamond ◆ glyph). Links: Program, Artists, Venue, Tickets, FAQ (anchor links to section ids #program #artists #venue #tickets #faq). CTA button "Get Tickets" (gold filled, scrolls to #tickets). Active nav state while scrolling: JS highlights the link of the section currently in view (use IntersectionObserver or scroll handler; active link gets gold color + underline). Mobile: hamburger button (aria-expanded, aria-controls) toggling a dropdown menu panel; menu closes when a link is clicked.

2) HERO (id="top", full viewport height, cinematic editorial layout): Background image https://source.unsplash.com/featured/2400x1400?museum,night with a dark overlay (layered gradients: near-black at edges, burgundy/navy tint) plus a soft golden spotlight radial gradient from top. Content: eyebrow "ARTIFACT: Museum Night"; huge serif headline "Museum Night, Reimagined" (with an italic gold accent word); supporting line; metadata row with date/time/place: "18 October 2026" · "19:00–02:00" · "The Old Gallery, Warsaw"; CTA buttons: "Get Tickets" (gold, href #tickets) and "Save to Calendar" (outline gold, id for JS .ics download). Small event metadata badges (glass pills): e.g. "One night only", "Limited capacity", "After-hours access". Scroll-down indicator at bottom.

3) CONCEPT / INTRO (id="concept"): thin gold divider, eyebrow "The Concept", serif title, short editorial paragraph: a few sentences about the museum opening after dark — velvet darkness, golden spotlights, quiet mystery, art-house cinema atmosphere; one night where the collection breathes. Then 3 feature cards (glass panels, hover lift): "After-hours exhibitions" (the permanent collection and a special nocturne exhibition open until 02:00), "Live performances" (ambient sets, projection art and sound sessions through the night), "Guided hidden-room tours" (small groups into storage rooms and the closed cabinet wing). Each card with a small gold inline SVG icon, title, 1-2 sentence text.

4) PROGRAM TIMELINE (id="program"): vertical timeline, hour-by-hour, gold spine line with dot markers, alternating or left-aligned items, scroll-reveal. Items (time — title, short description, location tag pill):
- 19:00 — Doors Open — "Welcome drink in the candlelit foyer as the galleries awaken." — Grand Foyer
- 19:30 — Curator Welcome — "Chief curator Dr. Anna Kowalska opens the night with a short address." — Main Hall
- 20:00 — Hidden Collection Tour — "Small-group walk through the storage rooms and closed cabinet wing." — Cabinet Wing
- 21:00 — Live Ambient Performance — "Marcus Thorne performs a slow-burning modular set among the sculptures." — Sculpture Hall
- 22:00 — Sculpture Hall Projection — "Julian Reyes maps light and archival film onto the marble collection." — Sculpture Hall
- 23:00 — Artist Talk — "Elena Voss and Sofia Lindqvist on light, material and the night." — Auditorium
- 00:00 — Midnight Gallery Walk — "A silent guided walk through the darkened galleries at midnight." — East Gallery
- 01:00 — Closing Sound Session — "David Okafor closes the night with a deep listening session." — Main Hall

5) ARTISTS / SPEAKERS (id="artists"): asymmetric grid of 8 cards. Each card: image (remote URL), name, role, short teaser line, "View details" button (opens modal). Use these EXACT image URLs, reusing the first two for cards 7 and 8:
1 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?gallery,art — Elena Voss — Light Installation Artist — "Sculpts with light, haze and shadow."
2 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?exhibition,lights — Marcus Thorne — Ambient Composer — "Slow modular soundscapes after dark."
3 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?sculpture,museum — Dr. Anna Kowalska — Chief Curator — "Keeper of the hidden collection."
4 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?museum,crowd — Julian Reyes — Media & Projection Artist — "Paints architecture with moving light."
5 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?art,installation — Sofia Lindqvist — Sculptor — "Stone, bronze and quiet forms."
6 https://source.unsplash.com/featured/1200x900?theater,stage — David Okafor — Sound Artist — "Deep listening and resonant spaces."
7 (reuse image 1) — Mira Chen — Performance Artist — "Movement pieces for silent rooms."
8 (reuse image 2) — Prof. Henry Walden — Art Historian — "Stories the collection tells at night."
ARTIST MODAL: accessible (role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby, focus moved inside on open, focus returned to trigger on close, page scroll locked while open). Shows image, name, role, a longer 2-3 sentence bio (write plausible bios per artist), session time (match timeline: Kowalska 19:30, Thorne 21:00, Reyes 22:00, Voss & Lindqvist 23:00, Okafor 01:00, Chen 20:30 "pop-up performance", Walden 23:30 "gallery talk"), close button (×), closes on ESC key and on backdrop click.

6) VENUE (id="venue"): two-column layout (text + map). Venue name "The Old Gallery", address "ul. Krakowskie Przedmieście 12, 00-325 Warsaw". Travel tips (arrive 15 min early; cloakroom at the foyer; last entry 23:30). Accessibility notes (step-free entrance on the north side, elevators to all floors, accessible restrooms, quiet room available). Parking / public transport notes (metro M2 Nowy Świat-Uniwersytet 6 min walk; bus lines 111, 180 to Plac Piłsudskiego; limited paid parking behind the gallery). Inline SVG map mock (dark panel background): a gold-outlined gallery block labeled "The Old Gallery", nearby street lines (thin muted strokes, 2-3 crossing streets with small labels), a metro marker "M" and bus marker "B" circles, an entrance marker (gold dot labeled "Entrance"), and a dashed gold route line from the metro marker to the entrance. SVG must be pure inline <svg> with text labels, styled with the palette.

7) TICKET TIERS (id="tickets"): 3 premium ticket cards (glass panels, hover highlight with gold border glow + lift; Curator Pass card visually elevated with "Recommended" gold badge and slightly larger/highlighted):
- Night Pass — €29 — features: "Entry after 19:00", "Main exhibition access", "Program access" — button "Select Night Pass"
- Curator Pass — €59 — badge "Recommended" — features: "Everything in Night Pass", "Hidden collection tour", "Reserved artist talk seating" — button "Select Curator Pass"
- Patron Pass — €129 — features: "Everything in Curator Pass", "VIP lounge access", "Signed event print", "Priority entrance" — button "Select Patron Pass"
Feature list items with small gold check marks (✓ or SVG). Note under grid: "Demo checkout — no real payment is processed."
TICKET CHECKOUT MODAL (accessible like artist modal): shows selected tier name + unit price; form fields: attendee name (text, required), email (required, email format), number of tickets (select or number input 1–6, default 1), live computed total price (€ unit × qty), required checkbox "I agree to the event terms and house rules", "Confirm reservation" button. JS validation: inline error messages under invalid fields (name non-empty, valid email regex, qty 1–6, terms checked); on success: close modal and show success toast "Reservation confirmed — N × Tier Name, €Total. Check your email for details (demo)." Also show a brief inline success state in the modal before closing OR just toast — but must include a clear success message. No real payment.

8) FAQ ACCORDION (id="faq"): at least these 6 questions as accessible accordion (button with aria-expanded controlling a region panel, smooth max-height/transition open/close, gold plus/minus indicator, only one open at a time is fine):
- "Is payment processed on this page?" — No. This is a demonstration landing page; the checkout is a mock and no real payment or booking takes place.
- "Can I arrive late?" — Yes, last entry is 23:30. Some guided tours have fixed start times and limited capacity.
- "Are photos allowed?" — Yes, without flash and without tripods. Some rooms are marked as no-photography zones.
- "Is the venue accessible?" — Yes: step-free north entrance, elevators to all floors, accessible restrooms and a quiet room.
- "Can I change my ticket tier?" — Upgrades are possible at the door subject to availability; just pay the difference.
- "How do I save the event to my calendar?" — Use the "Save to Calendar" button in the hero to download an .ics file and import it into your calendar app.

9) NEWSLETTER (id="newsletter"): glass panel with serif title "Letters from the museum", short line, email input + "Subscribe" button. Inline validation (invalid → red/gold error message under input; valid → success message + toast "Subscribed — see you in the dark."). Prevent default submit.

10) FOOTER: "ARTIFACT" logo, event credits line ("An after-hours concept by The Old Gallery · Program curated by Dr. Anna Kowalska"), social-style text links (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube — href="#" placeholders), copyright "© 2026 ARTIFACT: Museum Night. All rights reserved.", and small muted note: "Demo landing page — no real ticket purchase."

=== SPECIAL FEATURE — SAVE TO CALENDAR (.ics, client-side, no backend) ===
JS: on "Save to Calendar" click, build an ICS string with CRLF line endings: BEGIN:VCALENDAR / VERSION:2.0 / PRODID:-//ARTIFACT//Museum Night//EN / BEGIN:VEVENT / UID:artifact-museum-night-2026@artifact.demo / DTSTAMP:(generate current UTC timestamp) / DTSTART:20261018T190000 / DTEND:20261019T020000 / SUMMARY:ARTIFACT: Museum Night / LOCATION:The Old Gallery, Warsaw / DESCRIPTION:A cinematic after-hours museum event with exhibitions, performances, talks, and guided tours. / END:VEVENT / END:VCALENDAR. Create a Blob (type text/calendar), a temporary object URL, a temporary <a download="artifact-museum-night.ics"> click, then revoke the URL. Show a toast "Calendar file downloaded."

=== TOAST SYSTEM ===
Fixed bottom toast container; JS function showToast(message) creates styled toast (dark glass, gold border, ivory text), animates in, auto-removes after ~3.5s; used by checkout success, newsletter, calendar download.

=== JS QUALITY ===
All JS wrapped in an IIFE or DOMContentLoaded; query elements defensively (null checks where sensible); NO console errors; no external requests except the listed images; all interactive controls keyboard accessible.

Generate the ENTIRE file in one pass, complete and self-contained, roughly 1200-1600 lines, polished and consistent."}
